interest: This document illustrates the State Department's internal record-keeping and cross-referencing system under the 1910–1949 central decimal file, showing how specialized subject files like 894.5161 (Interest and Discount) often served as index registers redirecting researchers to broader periodic reports (894.00 P.R.). Substantively, the two indexed despatches capture two critical turning points in Japan's interwar monetary history: the tightening of credit in autumn 1931 just prior to Japan's departure from the gold standard, and the coordinated interest rate reduction by the Bank of Japan and semi-official banks in April 1936 following the February 26 Incident to facilitate deficit bond absorption and support Takahashi-era industrial and military financing.
overview: This file consists of a single State Department 'List of Papers' docket sheet for decimal file 894.5161, covering interest and discount rates in Japan between 1931 and 1936. The sheet indexes two diplomatic despatches received from the U.S. Embassy in Tokyo whose full texts were filed under the periodic report series (894.00 P.R.). The first entry records Despatch No. 379 of November 6, 1931, from Ambassador W. Cameron Forbes, reporting the Bank of Japan's announcement on October 6 raising its official discount rate effective October 5, 1931. The second entry records Despatch No. 1829 of May 13, 1936, from Ambassador Joseph C. Grew, reporting that the Bank of Japan and semi-official banks lowered discount and interest rates by an average of 0.37% annually on April 6, 1936, detailing the reasons given for the reduction.

subfiles.about: A State Department List of Papers docket sheet indexing despatches concerning Bank of Japan interest and discount rate adjustments between 1931 and 1936.
subfiles.summary: This single-page document is a State Department 'List of Papers' docket sheet for decimal file 894.5161 (Interest and discount - Japan). It indexes two despatches from the U.S. Embassy in Japan that were physically filed under periodic political/economic reports (894.00 P.R.). The first entry cites Despatch No. 379 of November 6, 1931, from Ambassador W. Cameron Forbes regarding the Bank of Japan raising its official discount rate in October 1931. The second entry cites Despatch No. 1829 of May 13, 1936, from Ambassador Joseph C. Grew regarding an average 0.37% annual reduction in discount and interest rates enacted by the Bank of Japan and semi-official banks on April 6, 1936.
